about.description_short: IAMGOLD is an intermediate gold producer and developer based in Canada with operating mines in North America and West Africa, including Cote Gold (Canada), Westwood (Canada) and Essakane (Burkina Faso). The Cote Gold Mine is among the largest gold mines in production in Canada, which IAMGOLD operates in a 70|30 partnership with Sumitomo Metal Mining Co. Ltd. In addition, the Company has an established portfolio of early stage and advanced exploration projects within high potential mining districts, including the large-scale Nelligan Mining Complex located in Quebec, Canada. IAMGOLD employs approximately 3,800 people and is committed to maintaining its culture of accountable mining through high standards of Environmental, Social and Governance practices. IAMGOLD is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: IAG) and the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: IMG).

analysis_md:
# IAG — IAMGOLD Corporation
Engine 5.4 pass-1 run, 2026-10-18. Canadian gold miner, 40-F filer reporting under IFRS in USD; common shares listed directly on the TSX (IMG) and NYSE (IAG). In scope (market cap est. $10.523B at $18.09, nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. Figures marked "search-cited" are from company releases found in web search; they are narrative context only and were NOT used in the scoring, because they are not in this run's code outputs.

## What it is
Mid-tier gold producer with three operating mines: Côté Gold in Ontario (70%, the flagship — construction through 2023, ramped through 2024–25, now at nameplate), Essakane in Burkina Faso (85%), and Westwood in Quebec (100%). 2026 attributable production guidance is 720,000–820,000 oz (search-cited, company Q2 2026 release). It sells a commodity at a price it does not set.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (40-F via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $2,852.8M; net income $732.3M; operating cash flow $1,142.6M; capex $293.5M; SBC $8.3M; diluted shares 581,700,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $840.8M = $1.45/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $1.45; latest FY OE total $840.8M). A genuinely cash-generative year — but it is the only one of its kind in the filed record, and it was earned at peak-cycle gold prices.
- The maintenance version is not computable: D&A is not separately tagged in this filer's IFRS facts (da tag null in dcf_numbers.json), so no NI + D&A bridge exists in the computed outputs. The conservative OCF-based figure is the series used throughout.
- **OE positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years** (key_numbers.md). OE/share history (financials_history.csv): FY2021 −$0.52, FY2022 −$0.71, FY2023 −$1.56, FY2024 −$0.14, FY2025 +$1.45. The trough years are the Côté construction peak — capex of $525.2M / $742.7M / $907.3M in FY2021–23 against a mine that produced nothing until its ramp. That capex is a real cost of a depleting-asset business, not an accounting quirk to normalize away: a gold miner must keep building or buying ounces to stand still.
- **Base used = normalized base: median of last 3 FY OE/share = −$0.14/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The median window (FY2023–25) sums to a negative figure (f_subtype: indeterminate, on the sum of the median window), so the engine's data gate refuses a DCF. No TTM base exists (see STALE_FY), and no base_override was declared: the single positive year was earned at the top of the gold cycle, and capitalizing it would be exactly the peak-earnings failure the normalized base exists to prevent. Sweep precedent for IFRS gold miners (AGI, EQX in this sweep) is the same: keep the normalized base and state the run-rate caveat plainly.
- Net debt (latest, FY2025): $227.9M (key_numbers.md), plus lease liabilities of $112.0M (dcf_numbers.json). Post-year-end deleveraging at current gold prices is real but is not in the engine's filed annual figures — see Flags/STALE_FY.

## Moat: 3/10 — weak; cost/reserve/jurisdiction only, no franchise
Justification: A gold miner is a pure price taker — no pricing power, no switching costs, no network effects; the only candidate advantages are cost position, reserve life and jurisdiction, and IAMGOLD is mid-pack on all three.
- Evidence (fundamentals.json): **ROIC proxy** ran 3.9% (FY2020), −3.7% (FY2021), 1.2% (FY2022), −0.0% (FY2023), 20.1% (FY2024) and 18.5% (FY2025) — below the cost of capital through most of the cycle and positive only when the gold price surged; that is operating leverage to a commodity price, not a franchise return. **Gross margin** over the same span: 20.2%, 7.1%, 15.4%, 12.6%, 33.7%, 42.3% — the expansion is the gold price plus the Côté volume ramp, not pricing power the company controls.
- FOR: Côté Gold (70%, Ontario): large long-life open pit now at nameplate throughput, with the Côté-Gosselin expansion as organic upside; Westwood (100%, Quebec): high-grade underground mine in a tier-1 jurisdiction; Balance sheet transformed post-ramp: net cash at June 30, 2026 with an undrawn revolver (Q2 2026 release), and buybacks begun — 21.5M shares repurchased in H1 2026 (interim statements)
- AGAINST: Pure commodity price taker: earnings are a leveraged function of the gold price; the FY2025 base year was earned at peak-cycle prices; ROIC proxy below the cost of capital through most of the cycle: −3.7% / 1.2% / −0.0% in FY2021–23 (fundamentals.json), positive only in the FY2024–25 gold surge; Mid-pack cost position: consolidated AISC $2,271/oz sold in Q2 2026 (company Q2 2026 release); Essakane (85%, Burkina Faso) supplies roughly half of attributable production — junta and security jurisdiction risk; Depleting assets must be replaced with heavy capex: $907.3M of capex in FY2023 alone; owner's earnings positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years; Dilution record: diluted share count compounding at 6.7%/yr (engine) to fund the Côté build-out
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 5.9 years, 15-year projection. Moot here — with no positive base there is nothing to fade.

## DCF — engine 5.4 final run (2026-10-18)
**No scenario table exists, by design.** The engine's data gate refuses to project a DCF off a non-positive normalized base: tier_by_numbers is F, f_subtype `indeterminate` (dcf_numbers.json basis: the sum of the last 3 fiscal years — the median window — is not positive), implied_irr_weighted and IV are null. Probabilities passed were the defaults (10/25/30/25/10); they change nothing when the base is negative.
- Growth sanity check (mandatory): the engine's growth blend of 38.82% (components: rev CAGR 5y 18.10% · rev CAGR 3y 43.82% · latest rev YoY 74.70%, key_numbers.md) is basis-break arithmetic, not a growth rate — the YoY and CAGRs straddle the Côté construction-to-production break (see BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT) and a near-doubling of the realized gold price. No miner sustains 38.8% OE growth off a completed ramp; the blend was not used, and under Tier F no growth input can change the verdict.
- The honest quantitative statement the numbers support: on the normalized base there is no price at which a DCF can be run at all. On the single best filed year (FY2025, OE/share $1.45), the OE yield at $18.09 is real but is one year at peak gold after four negative years. A buyer here is long gold and Côté's continued ramp, not long through-cycle owner's earnings.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): RESOLVED WITH THE CAVEAT STATED. ttm.py was run and failed as the spec predicts for an IFRS filer: "cannot compute TTM for IAG (CIK 1203464): ocf: no annual (FY) fact; sbc: no annual (FY) fact; shares_diluted: no annual (FY) fact; capex: no capex facts in companyfacts under any candidate tag" — ttm.py reads us-gaap facts only, IAG files ifrs-full, so the median base was used, as instructed. Interim context the engine cannot score (search-cited, company Q2 2026 release): H1 2026 revenue $1,887.0M from 406,600 oz sold at a $4,631/oz average realized price; net cash from operating activities $1,015.0M YTD; net earnings attributable to equity holders $610.2M YTD; net cash position of $52.2M at June 30, 2026 with the credit facility fully repaid; full-year attributable production guidance of 720,000–820,000 oz reaffirmed. The current year is running above the FY2025 base on both price and volume. The F verdict is therefore a verdict on normalized, filed annual numbers; it is not a claim that the trailing twelve months are loss-making at $4,000+ gold. Building a TTM base from interim filings is outside a worker's bounded authority (this run's code outputs contain no interim OE legs for an IFRS filer) — if a current-base read is wanted, that is a main-agent decision.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 6.7%/yr): REAL, and construction-financing-driven, not SBC-driven. SBC ran $5.1M–$8.3M/yr across FY2021–25 (financials_history.csv) — immaterial. The count growth is equity issued to fund the Côté build: diluted weighted shares went 484,600,000 (FY2023) → 545,900,000 (FY2024) → 581,700,000 (FY2025), with 591,144,545 shares outstanding at Dec 31, 2025 (dcf_numbers.json). The −5.00% growth adjustment (key_numbers.md) is already deducted in the blend. Direction has reversed post-ramp: the company repurchased 21.5M shares under its NCIB in H1 2026, taking shares outstanding to 574.3M at June 30, 2026 (search-cited, Q2 2026 interim financial statements).
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump in the last 5 yrs): NAMED — the Côté Gold construction-to-production break, plus a gold-price step-up. Revenue went $987.1M (FY2023) → $1,633.0M (FY2024, +65%) → $2,852.8M (FY2025, +74.70% latest YoY, key_numbers.md) as Côté poured first gold, ramped to nameplate (96,200 oz produced in Q2 2026 on a 100% basis, search-cited) and realized prices climbed toward the $4,631/oz printed YTD in 2026. A secondary item: the Bambouk asset sale contributed a $34.1M gain in FY2024 (FY2025 statements comparative column). Consequence: every CAGR in the blend straddles the break, the 38.82% blend is not a usable growth input, and no growth input was relied on (moot under Tier F).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024): RESOLVED — FY2024 net income of $847.8M vs OCF of $486.0M (financials_history.csv). The bridge is non-cash items inside net income: a $455.5M impairment reversal credited in FY2024 earnings and the $34.1M gain on the sale of the Bambouk assets (both per the FY2025 consolidated statements' comparative column, search-cited) — neither produced operating cash. The OCF-based conservative OE is not contaminated by them; if anything FY2024 shows the opposite distortion, with OE/share of −$0.14 because $558.6M of (mostly Côté completion) capex ran through the OE definition while the impairment reversal flattered reported earnings.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED** (×1.0): resolved under bounded authority (step 8d). judgment.json declares ads_ratio {ratio: 1.0, source: "Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-18), cover page: securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) are 'Common Shares, no par value', trading symbol IAG, New York Stock Exchange, with 591,144,545 shares outstanding as of period end — exactly the engine's DEI count", reason: direct cross-listing — the NYSE security is the common share itself (same class as TSX: IMG), not an ADS}. The engine applied it (×1.0) and make_score.py accepted it; no per-share figure changes.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The F is the method working as intended on a hard case: five filed years of owner's earnings contain exactly one positive year, and that year was earned at the top of the gold cycle after a $2.5B-plus construction program whose capex the conservative OE definition correctly charges. Normalizing that away is the point of the median base.
- What the F does NOT capture, stated plainly: (1) FY2025's $840.8M of OE is real cash (OCF $1,142.6M), not an accounting artifact, and H1 2026 interim prints run above it; (2) the balance sheet at June 30, 2026 is net cash (search-cited) versus the engine's $227.9M net debt at FY2025 year-end; (3) the Côté-Gosselin technical report update expected in Q4 2026 (search-cited) is a genuine expansion catalyst. Anyone re-underwriting this name on current numbers at $4,000+ gold gets a higher base — but at a through-cycle gold price the same math cuts the other way, and the filed record through a full cycle is what this pass scores.
- Watch items: gold price (the whole thesis), Essakane's Burkina Faso operating environment, Côté unit costs as the mine moves through pushbacks (Q2 2026 strip ratio 2.8:1, search-cited), and whether the new buyback survives a gold retracement.
